EnableDevMode.Name: Enable Dev Mode
EnableDevMode.Hint: Shows the 'Dev Sync' button (downloads the collected payload as JSON, for local use and development.) Off by default.

AllowPlayerSelfPublish.Name: Allow Player Self-Publish
AllowPlayerSelfPublish.Hint: Lets a player who owns a journal entry (Foundry's own Owner permission) see and use that entry's Publishing Settings, Post Settings, and publish controls themselves.  Will communicate the github token to their browser, so only enable this if you trust your players not to abuse it. Off by default.

DeploySite.Name: Set Up Your Site
DeploySite.Label: Setup Wizard
DeploySite.Hint: Create a world2web site on Netlify, Cloudflare, or Vercel from the site template.  Requires an account at that provider, as well as a GitHub account.

GithubOwner.Name: GitHub Repo Owner
GithubOwner.Hint: Your GitHub username or org, e.g. 'alice' in github.com/alice/my-campaign-site.

GithubBranch.Name: GitHub Branch
GithubBranch.Hint: The branch your host (Netlify/Cloudflare Pages/etc.) builds from.

GithubToken.Name: GitHub Personal Access Token
GithubToken.Hint: Fine-grained token.  Recommended to create a token with permissions to only this one repo, Contents: Read and write permission.

SiteTheme.Name: Site Theme
SiteTheme.Hint: A theme name (e.g. 'midnight') matching one built into the site template's own styles/tokens.css, or blank/'default' for the site's built-in look.

AllowThemeOverride.Name: Allow Visitor Theme Override
AllowThemeOverride.Hint: Lets site visitors pick their own theme from a dropdown, saved in their own browser -- overriding Site Theme above just for them. Off by default: Site Theme applies to everyone, and the dropdown doesn't appear at all.

SiteName.Name: Site Name
SiteName.Hint: Replaces "World2Web" as the site's name/branding (page title, homepage heading, breadcrumbs).

JournalsSegment.Name: Journals URL Segment
JournalsSegment.Hint: The URL segment for journals on the site, e.g. yoursite.com/<world>/<this>/<journal>/. Gets slugified automatically, so spaces/capitals are fine to type here. Defaults to "journals".

Notify.MissingGithubConfig: can't publish -- GitHub Repo Owner, Repo Name, and Token must all be set first. Check Configure Settings.
Notify.NothingToPublish: no journals are marked as published -- nothing to publish.
Notify.Published: pushed {posts} post(s) and {assets} asset(s) to GitHub, retracted {retracted} deleted page(s).
Notify.UpToDate: everything already up to date on GitHub.
Notify.PageTypeNotPublishable: "{name}" is a {type} page -- only text and image pages can be published.
Notify.NoCurrentPage: couldn't determine which page to publish -- see console.
Notify.DeploySiteSaved: GitHub Repo Owner, Repo Name, and Token saved. Try Publish to Web whenever you're ready.

Tooltip.PublishCleanPending: Published locally -- click Publish to Web to make it live (click here to unpublish instead)
Tooltip.PublishNeverPending: Unpublished -- click Publish to Web to remove it from the live site

Dialog.Title: Publishing Settings: {name}
Dialog.PublishLabel: Publish this journal to the web
Dialog.PublishHint: Unchecking this retracts every one of this journal's already-published posts from the site on the next publish (they don't get deleted from GitHub -- there's no way to -- but they stop showing up). Re-checking it later brings back whichever pages are still individually marked published.
Dialog.AuthorActorHint: Drag an Actor here from the sidebar, a compendium, or a scene token -- or type/paste its UUID directly (right-click it → "Copy Document UUID") -- to author this journal as that Actor. Name, portrait, and (system permitting) biography all come from it, and it wins outright over the name/image overrides below rather than combining with them. Lets a GM write in an NPC's voice, not just default to whoever owns the journal.
Dialog.AuthorNameHint: Ignored if Author Actor override above is set. Otherwise defaults to the first non-GM user with Owner permission on this journal, shown as their assigned character's name (or their own Foundry username if they don't have one). Falls back to "Game Master" if no player owns it. No biography in this mode -- there's no Actor to pull one from.
Dialog.AuthorImageHint: Ignored if Author Actor override above is set. Path or URL. Defaults to that same owner's character portrait, if they have one.
Dialog.RootHint: A "/"-separated list of folder names, e.g. "Campaign/Arc 1" -- placed between /journals/<world>/ and this journal's own address on the site, and each folder in the list becomes its own browsable page there too. Defaults to this journal's own folder hierarchy in Foundry.
Dialog.PostOrderManual: Manual (same order as this journal's page list in Foundry)
Dialog.PostOrderHint: Order of this journal's own post listing only -- recent-posts widgets and author/tag archives elsewhere on the site always show newest first regardless. For Manual: reordering pages here doesn't update the live site by itself -- click Publish to Web (or Dev Sync) again afterward to push the new order.
Dialog.PostAuthorActorHint: Same as the journal-level Author Actor override (drag an Actor here, or type/paste its UUID), but for this one post only -- wins outright over this post's own name/image overrides below. Leave blank to use this journal's own author (shown as the placeholder below) for this post.
Dialog.PostAuthorNameHint: Ignored if this post's own Author Actor override above is set. Leave blank to use this journal's own author (shown as the placeholder below) for this post -- no biography in this mode either way, same as the journal-level override.
Dialog.PostAuthorImageHint: Ignored if this post's own Author Actor override above is set. Path or URL. Leave blank to use this journal's own author's portrait for this post.
Dialog.PostTagsHint: Fully replaces this journal's own tags for this one post -- doesn't add to them. Leave blank to use this journal's own tags for this post.
Dialog.FrontImageHint: This post's featured image -- an Actor's UUID is NOT accepted here, just a direct path or URL (e.g. from Foundry's own file picker, or an external link). Never auto-derived from the post's own body content. Blank means no front image for this post -- there's no journal-level default to fall back to.
Dialog.DeployStep1Of3: Step 1 of 3: Name your site and choose a host
Dialog.DeployStep2Of3: Step 2 of 3: Create a GitHub token
Dialog.DeploySiteIntro: Pick a host below to open its own one-click deploy page in a new tab. Each generates a new repo from the World2Web site template under your own GitHub account and hosts it there -- both in one flow, on that host's own site, with its own deploy authentication handled behind the scenes (the separate Cloudflare API token this module's README mentions is for its fully-manual setup path -- it doesn't come up in this one-click flow).
Dialog.DeploySiteFirstBuildNote: Deployment may trigger automatically and fail with no content, but will publish successfully when you publish.
Dialog.DeploySiteRepoNameHint: At Cloudflare/Netlify/Vercel, make sure to pick the same repository name you used here.
Dialog.DeploySiteAlreadyConfiguredWarning: Heads up: GitHub Repo Owner/Name/Token are already set here (currently pointing at "{owner}/{repo}"). Continuing creates a brand-new, separate repo and site -- it won't touch your existing one by itself. But finishing this wizard afterward (step 3) will repoint World2Web at the new one, and it'll stop publishing to your current site -- which stays live at its existing URL either way, just frozen, not deleted. Only continue if you actually mean to switch sites (or want a genuinely separate second one).
Dialog.DeploySiteTokenIntro: Foundry needs its own GitHub token to push posts to your new repo -- none of these deploy flows create one for you, so this is still a separate step on GitHub's own site. The button below opens GitHub's token creation page with the right owner and "Contents: Read and write" permission already pre-filled -- under "Only select repositories," pick {repo} (there's no way to pre-select that part), then Generate token and copy it before continuing to the last step.
Dialog.DeploySiteSaveIntro: Paste in your new repo's owner, name, and the token you just copied -- this saves them directly, the same as the fields in Configure Settings.
